bucket_prompt: Create a production-ready 2D game sprite sheet for GRAY, a monochrome dark fantasy side-scrolling puzzle platformer in a decayed industrial sewer. Exactly SIX bucket sprites in a strict 3 columns x 2 rows uniform grid, identical size, identical front orthographic camera, identical bucket outer geometry and handle position in every cell, all bases precisely aligned within each cell. No text, no labels, no numbers, no arrows, no grid lines, no environment, no floor, no cast shadow. Isolated sprites on a perfectly flat solid bright magenta #FF00FF background for later chroma key extraction. Large clear margins between objects. Bucket design: squat trapezoid pail wider at open top and narrower at bottom, a thin arched carry handle with small grip, worn cast-iron rim and bottom band, rivets, just TWO slim vertical iron braces, large clear glass front revealing contents. Hand-painted grayscale material texture with sharp readable silhouette, restrained highlights, worn matte metal, subtle 2.5D volume but straight front view. Not cute, no pixel art, no modern plastic. First row: very dark iron bucket with BLACK paint, states left to right EMPTY, exactly HALF FULL at 50%, FULL at 100% just below rim. Second row: pale gray iron bucket with WHITE paint, same left to right EMPTY, HALF FULL, FULL. Empty cavity looks dark gray with a few faint glass reflections. Black liquid must read distinctly darker than empty glass; thin silver-white meniscus clearly indicates 50% and 100%. White paint is opaque off-white with a clearly visible horizontal meniscus, no blue tint. The HALF FULL surface sits halfway between inner bottom and open mouth, the FULL surface sits immediately below top lip. Opaque fluid hides rear surfaces only below its waterline; front metal braces stay above fluid. The gameplay is exactly two paint shots: first shot fills half and second fills completely. Every sprite must have the same unchanged frame, handle, rim, braces and silhouette so the three fill states can be swapped without jitter. Fine details should stay readable when downscaled to approximately 150x170 pixels per sprite. Sprites occupy most of their uniform cells with safe padding. High quality game asset, NOT a concept art presentation.
box_prompt: Create one production-ready isolated 2D game sprite of a heavy square cast-iron pushable crate for GRAY, a monochrome dark fantasy side-scrolling puzzle platformer inside an old industrial sewer. Front orthographic elevation, a square silhouette with only a very shallow top lip suggesting 2.5D volume, no isometric view or visible deep side face. Entire crate centered with padding. Thick worn metal border, small rivets at corners, two dark diagonal reinforcing steel straps forming an X across the front, small round iron boss at the center, understated downward triangular weight symbol pressed into center boss. Neutral MID-GRAY metal throughout, not a white crate or black crate: it is color-neutral in gameplay. Hand-painted subtly mottled cast iron with restrained gray edge highlights, pitted aged surface, heavy weight and readable silhouette, industrial dark fantasy aesthetics. NOT wood, not cute, not cartoon, not pixel art, not shiny chrome. Intricate enough to feel crafted but readable downscaled to 104x102 pixels. Isolated on a perfectly uniform solid bright magenta #FF00FF backdrop for later clean chroma-key alpha extraction. No text, no logos, no floor, no shadow outside sprite, no scene, no border around canvas. Single finished game asset.
